p033e.name: The Red Line's second paragraph by itself, try 5: the DeltaFosB sentence joined to the one it continues
p033e.text: So if you try to process trauma while you're above this red line, you're adding to the armor instead of taking it off. Above the line your functional IQ drops a lot, and stress chemicals called catecholamines flood the Nucleus Accumbens, a reward center deep in the brain, where they switch on DeltaFosB, the protein researchers suspect holds the armor in place. Only work on your trauma while you're under that line (what trauma therapists call your "window of tolerance").
p033e.diagnosis: from try 4 (#342: High 50, Low 14 over the DeltaFosB sentence, Medium 19 over the advice): the DeltaFosB sentence read Low in tries 2 to 4; it is a short sentence that only continues the one before through two pointers ("There they"), so it is joined to it, the way he joins short sentences (gate E368: ", where they switch on DeltaFosB")
p033e.decides: whether the join takes the DeltaFosB clause to High; the advice's Medium may follow it, as a short last line often does
p033e.tells: "instead of taking it off" (a contrast, though it answers what the reader expects processing to do); a long second sentence
p033e.human_tells: none to name: the words are mine and the post's
p033e.first_fix: payoff: the claim, then why (above the line), then what to do; join: the caveat into the clause it qualifies ("though the research on that isn't settled"); plain: "set off the making of DeltaFosB" for "transcribe new DeltaFosB proteins", "stress chemicals called catecholamines", "only work on your trauma while you're under that line" for "staying within a manageable window of tolerance rather than overwhelming activation"
p033e.humanized: the claim, then why, then what to do, in the reader's order; the packed second sentence split where "There they" carries on; the Nucleus Accumbens explained where the article first uses it ("a reward center deep in the brain"); catecholamines as "stress chemicals"; the caveat joined to the clause it qualifies; the advice an order, not "I'd ... your trauma", which read as the writer working on the reader's trauma
